audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Xerath 6 of 7 stages against a 52.04% Aurelion Sol winrate over 736 games, and the layers disagreed: phases[4..6].side read Skill/Skill/Skill while win[4..6] read Xerath/Xerath/Aurelion Sol.
audit.why: Xerath genuinely owns levels 1-5 on range alone (Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction both outrange the 750-unit Breath of Light). Level 6 evens it because Rite of the Arcane immobilises him, and the first-item window is a wash before Stardust pulls ahead.
audit.corrected: Xerath / Xerath / Xerath / Xerath / Skill / Skill / Aurelion Sol, proposed as matched full+content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes referenced 'Mage Fire' (not a Xerath ability), 'Comet of Legend' and 'Starsurge' (not Aurelion Sol abilities).
audit.why: Xerath's W is Eye of Destruction; Aurelion Sol's kit is Breath of Light, Astral Flight, the black hole and Falling Star / The Skies Descend, scaling off Stardust.
audit.corrected: All three fabricated names replaced and the spikes rebuilt around Rite of the Arcane's 5000 range, its 130/115/100s cooldown, and the Stardust curve.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two decisive channel interactions were absent, and wants.you[0] told the player to 'use E to block incoming Arcanopulse poke'.
audit.why: Aurelion Sol's E is a black hole — it does not block projectiles; minions do, and Arcanopulse is flagged projectile. The real interactions are that Shocking Orb (13/12.5/12/11.5/11s) is the only thing that cancels Breath of Light and Astral Flight, and that Rite of the Arcane immobilises Xerath for the whole channel, so Falling Star at 1250 range cancels it outright.
audit.corrected: Fixed in wants.you[0], breakdown.cooldowns, spikes[1], early, mid, whys[4] and dosFull[0].d.

audit.why: Xerath's punishable windows are numeric and specific.
audit.corrected: Shocking Orb 13-11s, Arcanopulse 9s / 80 mana at rank 1, Rite of the Arcane 130s at rank 1 now appear in breakdown.cooldowns, early and ahead.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane at 6 extends his range advantage into a global poke threat
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane roots him in place for its shots — Falling Star ends it early

edits.before: Full stacks and Comet of Legend finally let your global threat outscale his plateaued poke
edits.after: Full Stardust and The Skies Descend finally let your zone control outscale his poke

edits.before: Xerath's Arcanopulse and Mage Fire poke out-range your unstacked Q entirely, letting him zone you off CS and stack a gold lead before your orbit is threatening at all.
edits.after: Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction out-range your unstacked 750-unit Breath of Light entirely, letting him zone you off CS and bank a gold lead before your Stardust curve threatens anything.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane fires from absurd range and can catch you across the lane or even snipe you during a Comet of Legend recall window, giving him poke pressure your kit can't answer at 6.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane fires from 5000 units and can catch you across the map, but it immobilises him for the whole channel — Falling Star at 1250 range cancels it outright if you are in position.

edits.before: Once you're fully stacked with Comet of Legend online, your global pick threat and burst finally let you punish his positioning during fights, since his damage plateaus with items while your Q keeps scaling with every additional star.
edits.after: Once you're deep in Stardust with The Skies Descend online, your drag-and-zone threat finally punishes his rooted positioning in fights, since his damage plateaus with items while Breath of Light keeps scaling with every stack you bank.

edits.before: Xerath's Arcanopulse range simply outclasses your unstacked Starsurge, letting him poke you off CS and zone your farm from a screen away, and you have no real way to punish this until your own range and burst start to matter — expect to be behind on both gold and HP through the laning phase.
edits.after: Arcanopulse outranges your 750-unit Breath of Light outright, and Shocking Orb on an 11-13 second cooldown cancels the channel if you beam anyway, so farm from behind the wave and only start the burn once his E is spent — expect to be down on HP through most of the laning phase.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane at level 6 extends his poke advantage into a genuine global-range threat, letting him snipe you during recalls or punish overextensions from absurd distance, and this poke war stays firmly in his favor even as you finish your first item, since his damage is range-and-cooldown based rather than a stat check you can outscale quickly.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane at level 6 extends his poke into a genuine global-range threat, letting him snipe you during recalls from absurd distance — but the channel roots him in place, so a Falling Star or a jungler's arrival ends it and wastes a 130-second ultimate. That trade math holds right through his first completed item, so bait the channel rather than fearing it.

edits.before: It takes reaching full stacks with Comet of Legend online for you to finally turn the corner — your global pick potential and stacked-Q burst let you punish his positioning in fights even though his poke never stops being annoying, and by two-plus items your scaling ultimately overtakes his flatter, range-dependent damage profile.
edits.after: It takes reaching full Stardust with The Skies Descend online for you to finally turn the corner — your drag threat and stacked-beam burst let you punish his positioning in fights even though his poke never stops being annoying, and by two-plus items your scaling ultimately overtakes his flatter, range-dependent damage profile.

edits.before: Farm behind minions and use E to block incoming Arcanopulse poke
edits.after: Farm behind minions so they eat Arcanopulse before it reaches you

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Astral Flight has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb: 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s and the only cancel on your Q channel — start the beam the second it is spent. - Arcanopulse is 9s and 80 mana at rank 1: track his bar, not just his cooldown. - Rite of the Arcane is a 130s channel — cancel it with R.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by scaling honestly — Stardust is permanent, and Xerath's range edge stops mattering the moment fights happen inside your black hole.

edits.before: Ahead, compound it: shove with E executes, burn Xerath on every W rotation, and group early — your beam turns small mid-game leads into unanswerable objective control.
edits.after: Ahead, take his mana: shove with E, force 100-mana Arcanopulses onto waves, then W over and burn him while his bar is empty and Shocking Orb is still down.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Xerath wins by stunning you out of Breath of Light with Shocking Orb, then poking you off the wave from outside your range.

edits.before: His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Every second of beam on him is permanent Stardust — but Shocking Orb cancels the channel, so start it only once his E is spent.

edits.before: Xerath whiffs Shocking Orb (Stun) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Xerath whiffs Shocking Orb — you own the next eleven seconds of lane.

edits.before: That is Xerath’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: His Q costs 80-120 mana; a poke war you refuse is one his mana bar loses first.

notes: wants.you[0] contained a real mechanical error — it told the player to block Arcanopulse with E, but Aurelion Sol's E is a black hole with no projectile-blocking property. Fabricated names killed: 'Mage Fire' (Xerath's W is Eye of Destruction), 'Comet of Legend' and 'Starsurge' (neither exists on the current Aurelion Sol). Left the level-1 through 4-5 rows to Xerath: both layers already agreed there and the range gap justifies it.
